answer: Each identity is verified by a Wesolowski VDF: repeated modular squarings form a dependency chain, so later steps cannot begin before earlier ones finish. GPUs may run separate chains, but cannot parallelize one clone’s sequential work; every forged identity therefore adds its own physical delay and computation. This bottleneck raises the cost of Sybil attacks, like climbing a ridge against the tide, while the proof lets verifiers check completion efficiently.
